items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Johnny Wiggs, I had a series of lessons that he, uh, used to teach Charlie DeVore. Um, and I recorded, uh, about a dozen of those lessons.

ctx.x: So, um, I did, uh, record that Roy Palmer I got on trombone and later Kid Ory on trombone. And, uh, um, St. Cyr, of course, and Pops Foster, several bass players. Uh, uh, Ed Garland, Montuti, they call it. He was one of my very favorite musicians. He still plays in California. Well, anyway, I have about 20 interviews, uh, different instruments. Natty Dominic, um, on trumpet. Bunk would have been a logical one. He was already dead. I never did get Louie. I would have tried to get him sometime, although it's a…
And this is on the New Orleans Ensemble Stock.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: which I wanted to try to get Johnny Wiggs talking more about the different styles that they played pieces in and the dances

ctx.x: Yes. Right at the end of the line. You go to the end of the line and this place, the One Cent Club, it means that you buy one drink at the regular price and you get a second drink for one cent. It was during the Depression, of course. They had on big blue silk blouses with big long full sleeves, you know, sort of like clowns wear. Not that they were trying to make clowns out of them, but I mean, it was a special uniform they wore. A drummer, I believe it must have been, I'm not sure, unless I, until I look up my…
I heard that song as a white religious piece.
